source_text: 3 SATURNUS. Saturnusque senex si deus, deus quando senescit? Aut si deus erat, cur natos ille uorabat? Terroribus actus, sed quia deus non erat ille, Uiscera natorum rabie monstruosa sumebat. Rex fuit in terris, in monte natus Olympo, Nec erat diuinus; sic deum esse diceba<n>t. Uenit inops animi, lapidem pro filio sorbsit: Sic deus euasit, dicitur modo Iuppiter ille.
pass_a_gloss: Saturnus senex — si deus, cur senescit? Cur natos uorauit? Rex in terris; se deum dixit; lapidem uorauit; modo Iuppiter.
pass_b_english: And old Saturn — if he is a god, when does a god grow old? Or if he was a god, why did he devour his sons driven by terrors? But because he was not a god, he consumed his sons’ bowels in monstrous madness. He was a king on earth, born on mount Olympus; and he was not divine, but called himself a god. He fell into weakness of mind and swallowed a stone for his son. Thus he became a god; of late he is called Jupiter.
